description: Crucible's stack declaration: how each stack declares how its tests run. A plain JSON descriptor, readable with any runtime's standard library; it is not a JSON Schema and no JSON Schema validator reads it. Under each stack: `location` names the file and table its declaration lives in; `entry` describes one declared target (null where the stack reads no target entry); `fields` lists each field with the `values` it may take, its `default` and whether it is `required`. A `values` is a list of the exact values, a {"pattern": [...]} of templates in which <NAME> stands for any non-blank name, a {"board-listed": "codecs.<kind>"} codec name the board must list at run time, a {"path": {"holds": "<file>"}} directory that must hold that file, a {"list": {"min": <n>, "items": <values>}} list of at least `min` items each of the `items` form, a {"path": {"exists": true, "node_id": "::"}} path relative to the project dir that `exists`, optionally followed by the `node_id` separator and a node id, where the part before it must exist, or a {"path": {"is": "executable"}} path relative to the project dir naming an `executable` file. A `key` may carry `tiers`, the allowed first segment, and `label`: "non-empty", meaning the /<label> part, when present, is non-empty. An entry's `frameworkless`: "skipped" means the reader skips an entry with no framework; an entry that omits it reads such an entry as rust's. `requires` names a field that must be present (true) or must hold one of the listed values; `excludes` names the fields that may not appear beside it; `when` is a rule for one value. An `open` entry accepts fields it does not list; `refused` names the fields it never accepts.

bun.description: A bun project declares its targets in package.json under crucible.targets, one entry per script.

codec.description: the stream codec, which the board must list under codecs.stream

path.description: the one variable the shipped reporters read

junit.description: the script writes a JUnit report, either at the client's flag or at the path an env:<VAR> names

console.description: a view codec, which the board must list under codecs.view; only on a junit entry, and bun-console only with framework bun-test

coverage.description: only lcov, on a junit: flag entry of framework bun-test

package.description: package-level keys a bun project may no longer declare

package_dir.description: the directory holding package.json, when it is not the project dir

rust.description: A rust project declares its targets in crucible.toml, one [targets.<profile>] entry per nextest profile. An entry with no framework is rust's.

stream.description: the run streams nextest's output on stdout, the default

arduino.description: An arduino project declares its native test targets in crucible.toml, one [targets."<dir>/<target>"] entry per make target.

key.description: the native dir relative to the project dir, joined by / to the make target

stream.description: make writes crucible events to the file CRUCIBLE_STREAM names

maven.description: A maven project declares its targets in crucible.toml, one [targets.<tier>] entry per tier.

console.description: surefire-console; the board must list it under codecs.view at run time

python.description: A python project reads no [targets] entry; it declares its runner in crucible.toml [python].

go.description: A go project reads no [targets] entry; it declares its module dir in crucible.toml [go].

eda.description: An eda project declares its pytest targets in crucible.toml, one [targets."<tier>[/<label>]"] entry per run, and may name its interpreter in [eda].

key.label: non-empty
key.description: the tier, optionally followed by / and a non-empty label

paths.description: pytest paths or path::node ids relative to the project dir

python.description: the interpreter that runs pytest, relative to the project dir

skip_rule.description: crucible.toml [targets.<key>] is one flat namespace: a key holds one stack's entry. The rust, arduino, maven and eda clients skip an entry that names another stack's framework, and refuse nothing in it; the skip is decided on framework before any other field is checked. An entry with no framework is rust's, and eda skips it.

writer.description: A writer writes the stacks and fields it knows. On a schema version newer than it knows it still writes what it knows, warns naming the schema version, and is not blocked. It never removes a field it does not know. With no schema (no declaration_schema key in crucible-clients.json, or the file missing) it writes nothing it cannot check, warns, and is not blocked. It always writes framework, even where a reader has a default.
